title: Permissions Error: Permission Denied (Directory Traversal)
symptoms: ls: cannot open directory: Permission denied
root_cause: A user or service cannot access a file because either the file lacks read permissions (r), or more commonly, one of the parent directories in the path lacks the execute (+x) search permission required for traversal.
diagnostic_steps: Check file ownership and mode: ls -la /path/to/file
Check every parent directory's execute permission: namei -l /path/to/file
Check if user is a member of the required group: id <username>
remediation_commands: # Ensure parent directories have execute permission for traversal:
# Set read permission on the file itself:
# Or adjust ownership if appropriate: sudo chown <user>:<group> /path/to/file

title: Filesystem Error: Read-Only File System
symptoms: touch: cannot touch: Read-only file system
EXT4-fs error (device sdX): ... Remounting filesystem read-only
root_cause: The Linux kernel remounted the filesystem as read-only (ro) to protect against data corruption following disk I/O errors, SMART hardware failures, or metadata corruption.
diagnostic_steps: Check dmesg for kernel I/O or filesystem errors: sudo dmesg -T | grep -i -E 'remount|ext4|xfs|error|i/o'
Check disk SMART health if smartctl is available: sudo smartctl -H /dev/sdX
remediation_commands: # Attempt temporary remount in rw mode (if hardware is sound):
# If corruption detected, schedule fsck on next boot: sudo touch /forcefsck && sudo reboot
